Events.RelatedDescription: Opened issue ".NET 11 Release Candidate 1" (#444) at dotnet/announcements
Events.RelatedBody:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

# Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.19 | 9.0.20 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-x86) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Additionally, if you've deployed [self-contained applications](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/deploying/#self-contained-deployments-scd) targeting any of the impacted versions, these applications are also vulnerable and must be recompiled and redeployed. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-69806](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-69806) ### Acknowledgements Ky0toFu with Microsoft ### Revisions V1.0 (09/08/2026): Advisory published.

Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native can perform an out of bounds write while processing MSFZ PDB files. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/133438 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.8 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-122 (Heap-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.10.0-beta1.24272.1, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 10 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 9 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ### .NET 8 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native) | >= 17.12.0-beta1.24603.5, <= 18.9.0-beta1.26405.1 | 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET or Visual Studio. 2. If your application references Microsoft.DiaSymReader.Native, update the package reference to version 18.9.0-beta1.26405.2 or later. Once you have installed the updated runtime, SDK, Visual Studio, or package, restart your apps for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.1xx | >= 9.0.100, <= 9.0.119 | 9.0.120 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ### .NET 8 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 8.0.1xx | >= 8.0.100, <= 8.0.129 | 8.0.130 8.0.4xx | >= 8.0.400, <= 8.0.423 | 8.0.424 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-58649 – .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet watch BrowserRefreshServer does not adequately validate cross-origin WebSocket origins, potentially allowing IL and PDB information disclosure. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56166 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-346 (Origin Validation Error) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. ### Describe the bug This is a nasty tangle of problems, and I have kept them in one issue deliberately. There are two defects, and they are governed by the two options that drive the import fix, of which `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` is documented as defaulting to `true`, and `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups` as defaulting to `false`. The first is a gate that means the `IMPORTS` fix runs only if one of those two keys is explicitly set, so a project that sets neither gets neither the ordering nor the group separation that the documented defaults describe, but setting either one is enough to put the default of the other into effect. The second is that two specific actions only occur when the imports are reordered in the same run: removal of all blank lines by `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = false` and removal of misplaced blank lines by `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = true`. The reason they are tangled is that they cannot be told apart from the outside. A blank line survives for two unrelated reasons, and the tool produces identical output either way, so a reader cannot tell which bug they have hit. Every row of the matrix below is therefore a measurement of both defects at once, not of one. Splitting the report would mean each issue inheriting rows that are evidence for the bug described by the other. I have not found a way to partition the evidence cleanly, and I would rather hand over the whole matrix than half of it. What follows is everything I could pin down, for what it is worth. ### Steps to reproduce Run `dotnet format style` on a project with `disable`, once for each row of the five tables below: the usings from the second column, and the `.editorconfig` keys from the next two. ### Expected behavior Abbreviations: - `sys-first`: `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` - `separate`: `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups` Alphabetical, with the `System` group not first, and no blank line: | # | Starting usings | `sys-first` | `separate` | Expected (per docs) | Actual | | Why | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1a | `Other`

`System.Text` | ✅ | Same as `5g` but with `separate = true`, so a gap is added between the two groups. | ### Actual behavior See table above. ### Is this a regression? Either is enough, and the value can be the option's own documented default, so this asks for nothing beyond what the documentation already implies. `1a` sets neither key and leaves the imports untouched. `1d` adds only `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first = true` and they get sorted. `1b` adds only `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = false` instead and gets the same result, so the choice of key does not matter. Nothing reports that the `IMPORTS` fix stopped running, and the output is the same as for a file that needed nothing. Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/cli) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

[*Pull Request Create*](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/prcreate), a [MerlinBot](https://https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot) Extension, was used to automatically create this pull request. If you have any questions or concerns with this pull request, please contact [MerlinBot Expert DRI](mailto:merlinbotdri@microsoft.com).

Issues.Title: Assembly version for DispatchProxy shim is too low resulting in duplicate types for DispatchProxy
Issues.Body:
Create a new `netstandard2.1` library.
Add a reference to `<PackageReference Include="System.Reflection.DispatchProxy" Version="4.7.1" />`
Try to use `DispatchProxy`

Expected: 
`DispatchProxy` is resolved from `netstandard.dll`

Actual:
```
error CS0433: The type 'DispatchProxy' exists in both 'System.Reflection.DispatchProxy, Version=4.0.6.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=b03f5f7f11d50a3a' and 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51'
```


Build contains conflict message:
```
Encountered conflict between 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' and 'Runtime:C:\Program Files\dotnet\packs\NETStandard.Library.Ref\2.1.0\ref\netstandard2.1\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll'. Choosing 'CopyLocal:C:\src\dotnet\runtime\artifacts\bin\testPackages\cache\system.reflection.dispatchproxy\4.7.1\lib\netstandard2.0\System.Reflection.DispatchProxy.dll' because AssemblyVersion '4.0.6.0' is greater than '4.0.5.0'.
```

Other shims avoid this by setting the AssemblyVersion higher than that which was previously shipped.

Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

https://github.com/ygoe/NetRevisionTool

That utility is run as a pre/post build event and temporarily replaces placeholders in the AssemblyInformationalVersion attribute with runtime values (like repo folder name, commit ID, branch etc etc).

The completed assembly then has this info "burned" into it as we go forward.

.Net Standard is not working with this.

1. It seems to populatethe Package Version (in the project's Package section) with whatever we put into AssemblyInfo.cs for AssemblyInformationalVersion.
2. The version of the generated nuget package is always set as 1.0.0.

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs " (#1775)

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions" (#1777)

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.

With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Title: Support per-client project autoload initialization options
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- Allow `initializationOptions.autoLoadProjects` to override the CLI setting per LSP connection: a positive integer enables loading with that discovery limit, `0` disables it, and missing/null preserves the CLI setting. Clients sharing a daemon can configure loading independently.

This is supported in the copilot CLI - https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/set-up-copilot-cli/add-lsp-servers#configuration-fields


## Validation

- Ran `dotnet format whitespace --folder . --include <changed C# files>` and `git diff --check`.
- Built both affected test projects with `RunAnalyzersDuringBuild=true`.
- `AutoLoadProjectsInitializerTests`: 5 passed (including 3 representative invalid-input cases).
- `AutoLoadProjectsTests`: all 11 cases passed across runs. Both consolidated daemon cases passed in the initial run; a subsequent existing solution-restore test stalled, so the run was stopped and all 9 remaining cases passed on a separate run with a 90-second per-test hang timeout.

Confirmed separately in the current Copilot runtime source that configured `initializationOptions` are forwarded into the LSP initialize request; no Copilot changes are required.

Issues.Body:
Previously, no automated system ensure we were following `.editorconfig`'s `charset` settings (`utf-8` vs `utf-8-bom`). Over time, many files drifted from their config setting and had BOM present when not expected or vice versa.

This fixes all BOM drift and adds a CI step to enforce it, which runs against all files in about 5 seconds. Future improvements (automatic fixes, run only against changed files) can be added in a followup PR.

Issues.Title: Propagate StateWhenNotNull through lifted logical NOT in NullableWalker
Issues.Body:
Fixes #78432

## Summary

Propagate `StateWhenNotNull` through lifted logical NOT expressions (e.g. `!c?.IsTrue ?? false`) in `NullableWalker`.

Previously, dereferencing `c` in constructs such as:
``csharp
if (!c?.IsTrue ?? false)
{
    Console.WriteLine(c.IsTrue); // Emitted false CS8602
}
``
emitted a false `CS8602: Dereference of a possibly null reference` warning because `NullableWalker.TryVisitConditionalAccess` only checked for `BoundConditionalAccess` and rejected lifted `!` unary operators. This caused flow analysis to fall back to `Visit(leftOperand)`, discarding `stateWhenNotNull` and unconditionally merging the receiver state with the null branch (marking `c` as `MaybeNull`).

## Details

1. **`NullableWalker.TryVisitConditionalAccess`**:
   - Recursively handle `operand is BoundUnaryOperator { OperatorKind: UnaryOperatorKind.LiftedBoolLogicalNegation } unary`.
   - Propagate `stateWhenNotNull` from the operand.
   - If the operand post-state has conditional state (e.g. from `[NotNullWhen]`), invert `StateWhenTrue` and `StateWhenFalse`.
   - Pass `operand` (instead of `access`) to `VisitConversion` when conversions are present.

2. **`NullableWalker.VisitUnaryOperator`**:
   - Added `case UnaryOperatorKind.LiftedBoolLogicalNegation:` alongside `UnaryOperatorKind.BoolLogicalNegation:` to ensure conditional state is swapped under lifted logical negation in general flow analysis.

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests to `NullableReferenceTypesTests`:
- `NullCoalescing_LiftedNot_ConditionalAccess_01`: Positive scenarios verifying 0 diagnostics for `if (!c?.IsTrue ?? false)`, ternary expressions, chained conditional access, explicit casts, loop conditions, and comparisons (`== true`, `is true`).
- `NullCoalescing_LiftedNot_ConditionalAccess_02`: Negative scenarios verifying that `CS8602` is properly emitted when fallback values or comparisons leave the receiver nullable (`?? true`, `== false`, `is false`).
- `NullCoalescing_LiftedNot_ConditionalAccess_03`: Verifies conditional post-condition state inversion with `[NotNullWhen(false)]` and `[NotNullWhen(true)]` under lifted negation and null-coalescing.

All 3 new tests and all 33 existing `NullCoalescing_CondAccess` unit tests pass cleanly.

Issues.Title: Implement OnDemand Project Loading
Issues.Body:
Add on-demand project loading for language-server requests to files that are not yet part of a loaded project. This lets the server provide project-aware results without requiring every project in a workspace to be loaded first.

- For a requested file, search upward to the workspace-folder boundary and load the supported projects in the nearest directory containing project files.
- Load those projects’ transitive project references, coalescing concurrent demands.
- Defer read-only request resolution until loading completes, then use the loaded solution while preserving the request’s captured LSP text.
- Keep startup loading via --autoLoadProjects separate from on-demand loading. On-demand loading is enabled by default and is disabled when Dev Kit features are in use.

Issues.Title: Add formatting option for spaces within interpolation braces
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Add a new C# formatting option, `csharp_space_between_interpolation_braces`, to control spacing within interpolation braces.

The motivation is to allow spaces around interpolation expressions to be retained instead of always being removed by the formatter.

When enabled, spaces are normalized to one space:

```csharp
$"Hello, { name }"
```

When disabled, they are normalized to no spaces:

```csharp
$"Hello, {name}"
```

This follows the existing `SpacePlacement` behavior rather than `PreserveSpaces`, so the option defines a consistent formatting style instead of preserving arbitrary existing whitespace.

The default behavior remains unchanged.

## Testing

* `dotnet test .\src\Workspaces\CSharpTest\Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Workspaces.UnitTests.csproj`

Issues.Title: Don't report cascading CS0131 for invalid initializer member assignments
Issues.Body:
Fixes #81666

`[0]` inside `with { }` is parsed as a collection expression, so `[0] = 1` fell back to being bound as a regular assignment and reported CS0131 before CS0747.

Assignment members whose left side isn't a member name or indexer are now bound without reporting errors from checking that the left side is assignable, since CS0747 already reports the member as invalid.

Object initializers go through the same path, so `new C1 { P1 = null, (P1 ?? P2) = null }` loses its CS0131 too (`ObjectCreationFlow_34`/`_35`).

Issues.Title: [LSP] Allow explicitly defining which solution or list of projects the language server should load
Issues.Body:
## Main request
From standard command line usage, there appears to currently be no way to exclusively define either:

- A particular solution to load
- A list of projects to load

It would be very helpful if there was an easy way to specify these options when starting the language server from the command line. One may not always want to open **all** projects in a particularly large directory. 

While the server does define `solution/open` as an RPC command, this requires a given client to support it. That effectively means the only way to open a particular solution or set of projects is to use Visual Studio or VSCode - both of which have UI that at least allow choosing what solution to scope the language server to.


## Context on the matter

I often find myself opening projects containing multiple nested solutions - sometimes even ones that reference projects outside of the current solution directory.

While the feature of automatically loading any discovered projects is indeed useful when you only have a few, I regularly work in solutions containing **dozens** of C# projects in the same solution, with nested solutions containing multiple more. I don't want or need to load all of them, and I actually *could not* load all of them because some of the projects do in fact lie outside of the working directory (a layout both VS and VSCode have no complaints about loading).


What parts did load ended up loading far slower due to the language server needing to discover them rather than reference them from a solution. I was unable to use the language server for those particularly complicated projects until I made a script to wrap it and manually inject the `solution/open` command myself. With the ability to specify **just** a solution or **just** a set of projects, load times became much quicker, and dependent projects in other directories were loaded just as they were in VSCode.

## Additional info

Before the Roslyn language server was broadly usable, I used a [wrapper that contained this exact feature set](https://github.com/SofusA/csharp-language-server) I'm requesting. Unfortunately, it became deprecated once Roslyn's could function on it's own. I could have kept using it, but I feel this should be a feature in the official language server.

I also used to use [Omnisharp](https://github.com/OmniSharp/omnisharp-roslyn), which also has a way to define specific solutions or projects to load from the command line. However, I also stopped using Omnisharp since it takes about five to ten minutes to load those big projects I mentioned.

----

This is my first time making an issue here, and I opted to write this out manually since I didn't see an "LSP feature request" template. I also made sure to dig pretty deep in the source and various issues before making my own, but all the same I hope I didn't miss something obvious!

Thanks for the work put into this language server. It's the fastest I've used, and having these requested capabilities would make it ideal for almost any editor supporting the language server protocol.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[LSP] Allow explicitly defining which solution or list of projects the language server should load" (#85794)

Issues.Title: Special-case collection expressions of `ImmutableArray` of 1-4 elements
Issues.Body: `ImmutableArray<T>` already has special treatment in collection expressions world, e.g. `[]` is lowered as `ImmutableArray<T>.Empty`. However, construction of an array of 1-4 elements, which is most common in practice, [creates an array and then wraps it into an immutable array via `ImmutableCollectionsMarshal.AsImmutableArray(array)`](https://lab.razor.fyi/#43rDyMUVUJSfXpSYq5dcLHSXsbQ4My9dIbiyuCQ1V885PycnNbkkMz-vWM8zN7e0JDEpJ9Waiys5J7G4WAGqj6uaS0FBQQEu71hUlFhpk5lXYqfga6ihqWBrpxBtGGuNW5ERTJGOghE-dcZI6nQUjPEpNUFVqqNgEmvNVcvlxZRcHMXJ0dV75ensDAGWBMYKRgA). From performance point of view this is totally fine since we allocate the resulting array only once, but from the IL size point we can do better and use predefined `ImmutableArray.Create` factory methods, which exist for creating arrays of 1-4 elements without `params` array or any other overhead. This is a super trivial change that won't require much work

Issues.Title: [Navigate To] never considers the symbol under the caret
Issues.Body:
### Background

`NavigateToSearcher` takes the search pattern, the solution, the kinds, the active document and the visible documents. The last two are used only to decide which project and which documents are searched first, and for the secondary sort. Nothing in the pipeline looks at the caret, and no symbol is resolved: the search matches names of declarations taken from the syntax index.

### What that looks like

The caret sits inside a call — `MenuItem.Create (isFavorite = false, ...)` — and the user hits `Ctrl+T` and types `Create`, expecting the member they are looking at. What comes back is every `Create` declared in the solution, ordered by folder distance and parameter counts, with the one under the caret indistinguishable from the rest. On a large solution it is usually not on the first screen.

Go To Definition answers that exact question, but the user reaching for `Ctrl+T` has a name in mind and does not expect the name they are standing on to be treated like any other.

### Proposal

When the search begins, resolve the symbol at the caret in the active document — the semantic model for the active document is already warm, and the work is bounded by one document — and let its declarations sort to the top when the pattern matches their name.

For a language without a semantic model the same effect is available syntactically: take the identifier token under the caret and use plain name equality as the tiebreak.

Either way it is a tiebreak among results that already matched the pattern, so nothing new is searched and nothing that does not match becomes visible.

### Questions

1. Is caret context acceptable input for Navigate To, or does that break the "search is independent of where you are" model on purpose?
2. If acceptable, should it apply only to an exact name match, or also when the pattern is a prefix or camel-case match of the symbol's name?
3. Should it be an option, given that it changes the first result for the same query depending on where the caret was?

This is related to the ordering gap I filed separately about the secondary sort key, but it is a different question: that one is about proximity of *files*, this one is about the symbol the user is looking at.

Related #85790
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "[Navigate To] never considers the symbol under the caret" (#85791)

Issues.Title: [Navigate To] ranks a result from the active project no higher than one from across the solution
Issues.Body:
### Background

`NavigateToSearchResultHelpers.ComputeSecondarySort` (`src/Features/Core/Portable/NavigateTo/INavigateToSearchResult.cs`) orders results that match equally well by, in order:

1. folder distance from the active document,
2. parameter count,
3. type parameter count,
4. name,
5. the result's file name split on dots.

The folder distance compares `INavigableItem.NavigableDocument.Folders` — the folders a document sits in **inside its own project**. It never looks at which project the result belongs to. A file at the root of any project in the solution therefore has distance 1, exactly like a file at the root of the project the user is working in.

### What that looks like

On a solution with 128 projects, `Ctrl+T` for a common name (`Create`) returns dozens of exact matches whose names are identical, so the whole order comes from that key. The results the user sees are spread across unrelated projects, and the declaration in the project they are editing is somewhere in the middle. It reads as "the ranking is broken", although each of the five steps is behaving as written.

`RoslynNavigateToSearchCallback.AddResultsAsync` already passes `isActiveDocument` to the Code Search window, so a result *in* the active document is recoverable — there is simply nothing between "the active document" and "the whole solution".

### Proposal

Add the project to the key, between the two:

```
active document -> active document's project -> folder distance -> parameter count -> ...
```

The cheapest form is a leading component in the string built by `ComputeSecondarySort`: `0` when `activeDocument.Id == itemDocument.Id`, `1` when the item's project is the active document's project, `2` otherwise, leaving the existing components untouched behind it.

### Questions

1. Is project proximity wanted in this key at all, or is the project-blindness deliberate — for instance so that a solution-wide search does not bury a better match from elsewhere?
2. If it is wanted, should a referenced or referencing project rank between "same project" and "unrelated", or is the plain three-way split enough?
3. Would you rather this were a signal handed to the search window (next to `isActiveDocument`) than a change to the shared sort key, since the key is also used by the older Navigate To UI?

The helper is shared by C#, Visual Basic and F#, so whatever shape is chosen applies to all three. I am happy to write it once it is clear which one you want.

Issues.Title: Prevent CI quality monitor queue saturation
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- route irrelevant completed check suites and unmerged PR closures to unique per-run concurrency groups
- serialize only actionable CI quality investigations in a new `ci-quality-monitor-v2` group
- bypass the existing saturated `ci-quality-monitor` queue

## Why

Workflow-level concurrency is evaluated before `jobs.collect.if`. The old global group therefore queued every completed external check suite, including events that `collect` would immediately skip. One waiting run blocked the group, 100 pending runs filled the queue, and subsequent events failed before creating any jobs. GitHub then notified the users associated with those triggering events.

The new group remains intentionally serialized and finite. It could still reach its queue limit if more than 100 genuinely actionable investigations accumulate, but irrelevant check suites can no longer consume those slots.

## Validation

- Fork end-to-end dispatch succeeded: https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/36492857513
  - all eight jobs completed successfully
  - no issue was created in the fork
- `gh aw compile .github/workflows/ci-quality-monitor.md` using gh-aw v0.89.21
- `git diff --check`

> [!NOTE]
> This pull request description was generated with GitHub Copilot.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Prevent CI quality monitor queue saturation" (#56427)

This falls in the dotnet new template engine space.

Verifier version 33 no longer uses an MIT license on the NuGet package, which is what Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Authoring.TemplateVerifier currently uses. At this time version 28 is used, but I wanted to make sure there's some long term plannning for what to do down the road since this will pull a dependency in for users of Microsoft.TemplateEngine.Authoring.TemplateVerifier that may at some point start to require those users to have a license to use Verifier.

It would be nice to know what will be on the roadmap, if that means moving away from Verify, figuring out licensing, etc.

Issues.Title: Polish `dotnetup` changelog to provide breaking change notices in `self update`
Issues.Body:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I have read the [dotnetup documentation](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/tree/release/dnup/documentation/general/dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup issues](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues?q=is%3Aissue%20state%3Aopen%20label%3AArea-dotnetup).
- [x] I have searched for [existing dotnetup discussions](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/discussions/categories/dotnetup).

### Issue type

Feature request

### Description

During `stable` or even for `preview` consumers, we could have `self update` warn and wait https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55511 if a major patch version bump is included in the newer version. In this case there would be breaking changes. Ideally, we could show the most recent version's breaking changes and notify the customer during the update process to make this more seamless. We'd need to lab out how to connect that breaking change doc in a secure way to the self update mechanism, especially with the current arcade infra which won't be used in `stable`. Ideally we don't have to implement two different changelog mechanisms.

### dotnetup version

_No response_

### Issue type

Feature request

### Description

`dotnetup` may be `daily`, `preview` or `stable` (unreleased).

The property that conditions a `dotnetup` build like how the `sdk` has an msbuild property to determine its build quality label (e.g. `preview` or not) is not yet semantically meaningful. This means `dotnetup --info` may not show the proper label. `self update` also relies on this property - although it's challenging to see if an msbuild property can be properly evaluated from within the executable itself. We should avoid stamping another complex property such as build identity which was temporarily in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55511 commit history as this is unnecessarily complex.

Issues.Title: Upgrade gh-aw to v0.89.21 and recompile agentic workflows
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Upgrade all dotnet/sdk agentic workflows to the latest stable gh-aw release, v0.89.21, regenerate their checked-in lock files, and enable gh-aw's native weekly auto-upgrade notifications.

This fixes the `/tactics` workflow activation failure in [run 36448562305](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/36448562305), where gh-aw rejected the generated workflow because its v0.82.9 compiler is now blocked. The current compatibility list blocks v0.82.8-v0.82.15, v0.83.0-v0.83.5, v0.84.0-v0.84.4, and v0.85.0-v0.85.3; v0.89.21 is not blocked.

### Compiler versions

| Workflow | Previous | New |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `add-tactics-template-on-comment` | v0.82.9 | v0.89.21 |
| `parallel-safety-audit-command` | v0.83.1 | v0.89.21 |
| `resource-lock-refactoring` | v0.86.0 | v0.89.21 |
| `ci-quality-monitor` | v0.86.2 | v0.89.21 |
| `issue-monster` | v0.86.2 | v0.89.21 |
| `build-failure-analysis` | v0.87.1 | v0.89.21 |
| `build-failure-analysis-command` | v0.87.1 | v0.89.21 |
| `issue-monster-assigner` | v0.88.7 | v0.89.21 |
| `issue-triage` | v0.88.7 | v0.89.21 |

## Automatic upgrade notifications

- Adds `.github/workflows/aw.json` with `auto_upgrade: true`.
- Generates gh-aw's native `agentic-auto-upgrade.yml`, scheduled weekly at its deterministic repository-scattered time and also available through `workflow_dispatch`.
- The generated workflow installs the pinned current gh-aw release and opens or updates a deduplicated issue when a newer stable release is available. It does not automatically modify workflow sources or merge upgrades.
- The workflow is wholly generated and maintained by gh-aw, so it is exempt from SDK-authored workflow telemetry requirements and is kept unmodified.

## Preserved customizations

- Verified the PAT pool remains wired through the `copilot-pat-pool` environment and selected token override in every participating workflow.
- Verified the validation added by b0d2150015 remains in `shared/pat_pool.md`: configured PATs are authenticated before selection, invalid entries are ignored, and a configured pool with no valid tokens fails explicitly.
- Verified the auth/firewall workaround added by b5affd91a3 remains present: affected workflows continue to use `tools.cli-proxy: true` and `github.mode: gh-proxy`, and detection/agent jobs retain the pooled-token dependency.
- Preserved the required `DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_SESSIONID` value in every SDK-authored generated agentic workflow; sources that did not previously declare it now do.

## Notable generated changes

- Copilot CLI engine version advances to 1.0.87.
- gh-aw setup advances to v0.89.21, with refreshed SHA-pinned GitHub Actions and firewall/MCP container images. Older cache restore/save setup steps are no longer emitted where the new compiler does not need them.
- The custom binlog MCP image can now be digest-qualified. It is pinned to `sha256:95afa9e51653d4ec64bb45d3d3d4d496e650fd6b3b7a305f58592a8f01127225` in source and generated locks instead of being pulled by mutable tag.
- The obsolete `sandbox.agent.sudo: false` field in `issue-monster` was removed by the v0.89.21 codemod; the new runtime profile retains non-root sandbox behavior by default.
- The compiler adds default agent/detection timeouts, stricter slash-command event gating (including CR line endings), queue semantics on workflows using the default concurrency group, OpenTelemetry environment plumbing, and updated conclusion guardrail handling.
- Generated least-privilege permissions are reshaped in a few jobs (for example, safe-output jobs drop unnecessary `contents: read`; activation/conclusion jobs receive the scopes required by current generated behavior). Source permissions, triggers, safe-output policies, tools, repository integrity policies, and network allowlists remain unchanged.
- `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` now contains the v0.89.21 setup and setup-cli action pins.

## Validation

All nine workflow sources and the repository-level gh-aw configuration pass:

```text
gh aw compile --strict --approve --no-check-update \
  --schedule-seed dotnet/sdk --action-mode action --action-tag v0.89.21 \
  --validate --no-emit
```

The command completed successfully. Existing warnings about missing `concurrency.job-discriminator` on several `workflow_dispatch` entry points, non-centralized slash-command routing, and the source-pinned `actions/checkout@v7.0.0` in `issue-monster` remain unchanged and are unrelated to this upgrade.

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Defer package help to the managed CLI in AOT mode
Issues.Body:
Manual backport of #56417 to release/11.0.1xx. The automatic backport failed because of merge conflicts.

### Summary

The dotnet CLI's AOT mode hid help output for package-management-related commands due to a gap in the fallback logic that delegated to the managed CLI implementation.

### Customer Impact

Customers that were looking for information about package-related commands could not see it until/unless they knew to run the non-AOT CLI via setting an environment variable. The commands themselves would work, just help output was missing.

### Regression?

Yes, since 11 preview 7.

### Testing

New tests have been added to the AOT parser to ensure that the managed fallback is used when these commands are requested at all. 

### Risk

**Low** - we already use this mechanism for other commands that need managed fallback at this point in time.

Issues.Title: Defer package/nuget help to the managed CLI in AOT mode
Issues.Body:
## Problem

With the AOT CLI enabled, `dotnet package --help` does not list `update`, and `dotnet package update --help` prints the parent `package` help. Both differ from the output with `DOTNET_CLI_ENABLEAOT=false`.

## Root cause

- `package update` is added to the command tree only on the managed path, by `NuGetCommands.Add` in `ConfigureManagedActions`. The static `PackageCommandDefinition`, and the tree built from it on the AOT path, does not have it. See #52661.
- `NativeEntryPoint` falls back to the managed CLI when the parse result has errors. But System.CommandLine suppresses the unknown-subcommand error when `--help` is present. For `package update --help`, the parse gives `HelpAction`, `UnmatchedTokens=[update]` and `Errors=0`. So the AOT path rendered the static parent help and did not fall back.

## Fix

Add `rootCommand.PackageCommand` to the commands that `AotPrintHelpAction` defers to the managed CLI. `new` and `test` are already on that list.

## Other managed-only tree changes

I checked every place where the managed path changes the command tree or its help:

- **`new`:** the managed CLI replaces the command with a template-engine version. Help was already deferred.
- **`test`:** in MTP mode, help comes from the test application. Help was already deferred.
- **`nuget why`:** needs no change. Help for anything under `nuget` goes to `DotnetHelpBuilder`, which forwards the arguments (`why --help`) to the out-of-process NuGet CLI in both modes. A new test checks that this parse stays in the `nuget` tree with its tokens.
- **Other `ConfigureCommand` calls:** they only add actions or completion sources, which help doesn't show.

## Tests

- Added `InvokePackageHelp_FallsBackToManaged` for `package --help`, `package update --help` and `package add --help`. With the fix reverted, these cases fail.
- Added `ParseNuGetWhyHelp_ResolvesToNuGetTreeForForwarding`.
- All 62 `AotParserTests` pass.

## User-visible change

In AOT mode, help for the whole `package` subtree now comes from the managed CLI. It matches the non-AOT output and is slower than AOT-rendered help.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "Defer package/nuget help to the managed CLI in AOT mode" (#56417)

Issues.Title: `dotnet format`: IMPORTS fix ignores documented option defaults and grouping
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug This is a nasty tangle of problems, and I have kept them in one issue deliberately. There are two defects, and they are governed by the two options that drive the import fix, of which `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` is documented as defaulting to `true`, and `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups` as defaulting to `false`. The first is a gate that means the `IMPORTS` fix runs only if one of those two keys is explicitly set, so a project that sets neither gets neither the ordering nor the group separation that the documented defaults describe, but setting either one is enough to put the default of the other into effect. The second is that two specific actions only occur when the imports are reordered in the same run: removal of all blank lines by `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = false` and removal of misplaced blank lines by `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups = true`. The reason they are tangled is that they cannot be told apart from the outside. A blank line survives for two unrelated reasons, and the tool produces identical output either way, so a reader cannot tell which bug they have hit. Every row of the matrix below is therefore a measurement of both defects at once, not of one. Splitting the report would mean each issue inheriting rows that are evidence for the bug described by the other. I have not found a way to partition the evidence cleanly, and I would rather hand over the whole matrix than half of it. What follows is everything I could pin down, for what it is worth. ### Steps to reproduce Run `dotnet format style` on a project with `disable`, once for each row of the five tables below: the usings from the second column, and the `.editorconfig` keys from the next two. ### Expected behavior Abbreviations: - `sys-first`: `dotnet_sort_system_directives_first` - `separate`: `dotnet_separate_import_directive_groups` Alphabetical, with the `System` group not first, and no blank line: | # | Starting usings | `sys-first` | `separate` | Expected (per docs) | Actual | | Why | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1a | `Other`

Issues.Title: Avoid redundant dataflow in security analyzers
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> This PR description was drafted with AI assistance.

Fixes dotnet/sdk#56413.

The crypto rules were running whole-method dataflow for each literal byte-array source, even in generated methods that never call a relevant cryptographic API. With thousands of call sites, that repeats expensive work without a possible diagnostic. This change first checks whether a sink is reachable (including through helpers), skips sink-free methods, and runs taint analysis once per method instead of once per source. Value-content analysis is omitted when neither source recognition nor control-flow decisions need it; ambiguous cases still use the original full analysis. The reachability checks conservatively account for implicit calls, initializers, branches, and recursive helpers rather than assuming a simple source-operation walk covers the CFG.

The same approach avoids value-content flow in property-set rules unless a mapped constructor, property write, or relevant control-flow path requires it. Value-independent constructor overloads can be mapped directly, while value-dependent ones retain flow. Direct constant checks for `AppContext.SetSwitch` and Azure `SharedAccessProtocol` avoid building dataflow for already-known arguments.

Targeted local reproductions (not general speedup guarantees) measured the 2,048-call CA5390/CA5403 case at about **128s before vs. 2.3-2.5s after**, a sink-free SQL CA3001 case at **1.209s vs. 0.014s**, and a CA2329/CA2330 property-set case at **40.787s vs. 1.313s**. The analyzer-free build of the crypto reproduction was **0.4-0.5s**, so this reduces rather than eliminates analyzer overhead.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Avoid redundant dataflow in security analyzers" (#56415)

Issues.Title: Reduce CA1508 analysis cost for local-function calls
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> This pull request description was drafted with AI assistance.

Related to #56412.

Local-function calls were excluded from the existing interprocedural entry-state trimming, so each call cloned and reanalyzed unrelated caller state. Across many calls, that work could dominate analysis time.

Enable trimming for directly invoked local functions when their flow state is safe to analyze. Keep state reachable through captures, parameters, receiver, static state, and tracked aliases; conservatively use the full state when safety cannot be established. Distinguish trimmed call results so updates preserve tracked-state semantics, while full-state calls retain their existing replacement behavior. Memoize successfully scanned static-local bodies to avoid rescanning shared function graphs.

Also stop CA1508's enclosing-method candidate scan at nested functions, whose bodies have separate control-flow graphs. On a related 548-call reproducer, CA1508 analyzer time fell from 41.4 seconds to roughly 5–7 seconds.

Issues.Title: [wasm] Default R2R inlining/debug-info stripping for browser and wasi RIDs
Issues.Body:
### Why

The CoreCLR WebAssembly runtime does not consume ReadyToRun inlining info, and inline tracking is disabled on wasm (dotnet/runtime#134690). dotnet/runtime#134690 adds `--strip-inlining-info` / `--strip-debug-info` defaults for `browser-` / `wasi-` RIDs, but only in two places: the runtime repo's own copy of `Microsoft.NET.CrossGen.targets` (used only for in-repo builds and tests) and `crossgen-corelib.proj`. User apps published with the SDK get no stripping. In dotnet/runtime#134618 it was requested that the wasm pack not add its own `--strip-debug-info` ([discussion](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/134618#discussion_r4109996255)), so the SDK is where this default belongs.

Size impact measured in dotnet/runtime#134689: stripping debug info alone reduced browser-wasm R2R images of CoreLib, System.Text.Json, System.Linq and System.Collections by 2.4% raw, 7.1% gzip and 9.4% brotli.

### What changed

- `Microsoft.NET.CrossGen.targets`: add `_IsWasmRid` (`browser-*` / `wasi-*`) and extend the existing Apple mobile defaults so `PublishReadyToRunStripInliningInfo` and `PublishReadyToRunStripDebugInfo` default to `true` for wasm RIDs. The gating matches Apple (#53514, #54529):
  - not `Configuration=Debug`
  - `DebuggerSupport != true`
  - an explicit user value wins
- `PublishReadyToRunStripILBodies` is **not** defaulted for wasm. CoreCLR wasm falls back to the interpreter for methods that aren't precompiled (NYI/SIMD methods compiled with `JitWasm*NyiToR2RUnsupported`, and generics outside the version bubble), so IL bodies must be kept.
- `PublishReadyToRunEmitSymbols` is unchanged. The SDK has no default for it (an empty value is treated as false), so there is nothing to add for wasm.

### Differences from the runtime repo's targets copy

The runtime repo's copy (dotnet/runtime#134690) uses `'$(PublishReadyToRunStrip*)' != 'false'`, with no Debug or `DebuggerSupport` gating. This PR follows the SDK's existing Apple pattern instead, so Debug and debugger-enabled publishes keep the metadata.

### Testing

Added `It_defaults_readytorun_strip_options_by_runtime_identifier` to `GivenThatWeWantToPublishReadyToRun`. It evaluates `PublishReadyToRunCrossgen2ExtraArgs` and `PublishReadyToRunStripILBodies` for:

- ios-arm64 Release and Debug (baseline; the Apple defaults had no test before)
- browser-wasm and wasi-wasm, each in Release, Debug, and Release with `DebuggerSupport=true`
- browser-wasm Release with `PublishReadyToRunStripDebugInfo=false` (explicit opt-out)
- linux-x64 Release (unaffected)

Local results on macOS arm64 after `./build.sh`:
- the new test: 10 of 10 passed
- the full `GivenThatWeWantToPublishReadyToRun` class: 36 total, 32 passed, 4 skipped (existing skips), 0 failed

### User-visible change

Release `PublishReadyToRun` publishes for `browser-*` / `wasi-*` now pass `--strip-inlining-info --strip-debug-info` to crossgen2 by default. Opt out with `-p:PublishReadyToRunStripInliningInfo=false` / `-p:PublishReadyToRunStripDebugInfo=false`.

> [!NOTE]
> This PR description and change were generated with the assistance of GitHub Copilot (AI).
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "[wasm] Default R2R inlining/debug-info stripping for browser and wasi RIDs" (#56411)
