Issues.Title: Share the Azure Monitor telemetry storage directory between managed and AOT CLI
Issues.Body:
Follow-up to dotnet/sdk#56274.

# Problem

The Azure Monitor exporter names its persistent storage sub directory by hashing `instrumentationKey;userName;processName;AppContext.BaseDirectory`. `dotnet.dll` and `dotnet-aot` have different base directories, so their telemetry lands in two separate directories. The managed side runs less often, rarely drains its own backlog, and that telemetry is lost.

# Change

Azure added the `Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter.StorageSubDirectory` AppContext value for us in Azure/azure-sdk-for-net#63337 (fixes Azure/azure-sdk-for-net#62997). `TelemetryClient` now sets it to `dotnet-cli`. `TelemetryClient.cs` is compiled into both `dotnet` and `dotnet-aot`, so one line covers both entry points. The instrumentation key and user name still contribute to the hash, so different users and resources remain isolated.

- `documentation/project-docs/telemetry.md` describes the shared directory.
- New E2E test `ItDrainsTelemetryPersistedByTheOtherEntryPoint`, run in both directions: one entry point persists telemetry, then the other leases the same blob from the same directory to upload it. With the `SetData` line removed, both cases fail because the directories differ.

# ⚠️ Temporary commit - do not merge as is

No released exporter contains the feature yet, and Azure's dev feed has no recent builds. Commit `adda62ab817` vendors `Azure.Monitor.OpenTelemetry.Exporter` `1.10.0-alpha.sdklocal.20260924`, built from Azure/azure-sdk-for-net@8c4894ed16ff8fced2db5613c20540ff4301e950, in `eng/temp-packages` behind a local feed in `NuGet.config`. Its dependency set is identical to 1.9.0.

Once Azure releases a version with the feature: revert that commit and bump `AzureMonitorOpenTelemetryExporterPackageVersion` in `eng/Versions.props`.

# Validation

- `PersistentStorageTelemetryE2ETests` and `TelemetryClientTests` (33 tests) pass.
- `Microsoft.DotNet.Cli.Telemetry.Tests` passes.
- Manually confirmed that `dotnet exec dotnet.dll --help` and AOT `dotnet --help` write to the same sub directory.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Share the Azure Monitor telemetry storage directory between managed and AOT CLI" (#56409)

Issues.Title: Accept `dotnet run -p` as a short form of `--project`
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`dotnet run -p MyApp` already runs that project. It then prints a warning telling you to type `--project` instead. That warning has been there since .NET 6.

People asked for the short form to stay. See [dotnet/sdk#22792](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/22792). Typing `--project` is a real nuisance for a command used many times a day, and the warning is written to normal program output, so `dotnet run -p MyApp` breaks tools that read that output. A follow-up on the same issue in May 2026 pointed out that five years later the warning is still there.

This change makes `-p` a supported short form of `--project` on `dotnet run` and removes the warning.

A value that contains `=` is still a build property, the same way `-p` works on `dotnet build` and `dotnet publish`:

- `dotnet run -p MyApp` runs that project
- `dotnet run -p:Configuration=Release` passes a build property
- `dotnet run -p Configuration=Release` passes a build property

That request was closed because using `-p` for both the project and a build property was considered a mistake. This change does not take the property use away. The command has accepted both forms the whole time. The only difference is that a plain project path no longer comes with a warning.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Accept `dotnet run -p` as a short form of `--project`" (#56408)

Issues.Title: [DoNotParallelize] Narrow GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading serialization to the CWD-mutating test
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Moves the class-level `[DoNotParallelize]` on `GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading` to the one test that mutates the process-wide current directory.

`ItResolvesRelativeRuntimeGraphPathAgainstProjectDirectory` changes `Environment.CurrentDirectory` to prove that `PickBestRid` resolves a relative `RuntimeGraphPath` through `TaskEnvironment`. Other tests in the assembly read the current directory without declaring a shared resource lock, so a method-level `[ResourceLock]` would not protect those readers. Method-level `[DoNotParallelize]` safely runs only the mutating test in the serial tail while the other tests in the class remain eligible for normal class-level parallel execution.

## Validation

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe scripts\RunTests.cs -- --project test\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests\Microsoft.NET.Build.Tasks.Tests.csproj --filter "FullyQualifiedName~GivenAPickBestRidMultiThreading" --repeat 5 --skip-redist-check
```

Result: all 4 tests passed in each of 5 runs; the project built with 0 warnings and 0 errors.

> Automated by the [ResourceLock refactoring](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/36041158741/agentic_workflow) workflow.

Issues.Title: Validate workload --source feeds before acquiring manifests
Issues.Body:
Fixes #29078

### Context

When `dotnet workload install` / `dotnet workload update` is given a `--source` URL that isn't a NuGet feed (for example `--source https://randomfox.ca/`), the SDK goes on to query every workload manifest package against it and prints a confusing error per manifest, such as:

```
Failed to update the advertising manifest microsoft.net.sdk.maccatalyst: Failed to fetch results from V2 feed at
'https://randomfox.ca/FindPackagesById()?id='microsoft.net.sdk.maccatalyst.manifest-7.0.200'&semVerLevel=2.0.0'
with following message : Response status code does not indicate success: 404 (Not Found)..
```

As suggested in https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/29078#issuecomment-2098513814, this validates the `--source` arguments up front, before any work is done, and fails with a single clear error.

### Changes Made

- Added `WorkloadPackageSourceValidator`, which checks each HTTP source passed via `--source`:
  - **V3 sources** (URLs ending in `.json`) must return a valid service index. This uses NuGet's `ServiceIndexResourceV3`, which already validates the document.
  - **V2 sources** must return an OData service document (`<service>` root element). NuGet's own `ODataServiceDocumentResourceV2Provider` only checks for a success status code, so any web page would otherwise be accepted as a V2 feed.
- `workload install` and `workload update` call the validator at the start of `Execute()`.
- Validation is skipped for:
  - local folder sources
  - `--from-cache`, where no source is queried
  - `--ignore-failed-sources`
- Added two localized strings, with `.xlf` files regenerated via `/t:UpdateXlf`.

Before:

```
> dotnet workload update --source https://randomfox.ca/
Failed to update the advertising manifest microsoft.net.sdk.android: Failed to fetch results from V2 feed at 'https://randomfox.ca/FindPackagesById()?id=...' ... 404 (Not Found)..
Failed to update the advertising manifest microsoft.net.sdk.ios: ...
...
```

After:

```
> dotnet workload update --source https://randomfox.ca/
The package source 'https://randomfox.ca/' is not a NuGet feed. Make sure the value passed to --source is the URL of a NuGet feed, for example 'https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json'.

> dotnet workload update --source https://example.com/index.json
Unable to load the package source 'https://example.com/index.json'. Make sure the value passed to --source is the URL of a NuGet feed and that it can be reached. Unable to load the service index for source https://example.com/index.json.
```

**User-visible behavior change:** an invalid `--source` is now a user error (non-zero exit code) reported before any manifests are downloaded. Valid feeds such as `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json` and `https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/` pass validation as before.

This PR covers the first case in the issue discussion: the source is not a feed. The second case, where the feed is valid but doesn't contain the requested workload packages, is unchanged.

### Testing

- New `WorkloadPackageSourceValidatorTests` (12 tests). They use a loopback `HttpListener` to cover:
  - a valid V2 service document
  - an HTML page served as a V2 source
  - a non-index `index.json` served as a V3 source
  - an HTTP 404
  - local folder, blank, and null sources
  - `IsODataServiceDocument` on a range of payloads
- Ran `GivenDotnetWorkloadInstall`, `GivenDotnetWorkloadUpdate` and `GivenWorkloadManifestUpdater` locally: 115 passed, 5 skipped, 3 failed.
  - The 3 failures (`GivenWorkloadUpdateAcrossFeatureBandsItUpdatesPacks` ×2, `GivenWorkloadInstallItTreatsPreviewsAsSeparateFeatureBands`) fail the same way on `main` without this change, and none of them use `--source`.
- Checked manually with the locally built SDK against `https://example.com/`, `https://randomfox.ca/`, `https://example.com/index.json`, `https://api.nuget.org/v3/index.json` and `https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/`.

### Note

While testing, I noticed `dotnet workload update --source https://www.nuget.org/api/v2/ --print-download-link-only` throws a `NullReferenceException`. It reproduces on the current SDK without this change, so it's not related to this PR. It looks like `NuGetPackageDownloader.GetPackageUrl` assumes a V3 service index. I'm happy to open a separate issue for it.

Issues.Title: Add an agent workflow to identify potentially stale references in Ignore attributes, TODOs, and workarounds
Issues.Body:
## Problem

Tests marked with `[Ignore]` referencing a GitHub issue or pull request, along with TODO comments and temporary workarounds tied to a blocker URL, can remain in that state long after the referenced issue is resolved or the PR is merged, with nothing prompting revalidation.

## Description

Adds a maintenance workflow, `stale-reference-check`, that runs on a schedule to find code references to stale issues and log follow-up issues to clean up.

- **Deterministic collection**: locates `Ignore` attributes, TODOs, and workaround comments with a nearby GitHub issue/PR URL.
- **Bounded agent interpretation**: lets an AI agent classify each candidate through a local, bearer-token-gated MCP source server that only exposes pre-validated, paginated text - the agent never queries GitHub or writes issues directly.
- **Validation and caching**: strict validation of every interpretation result and action against trusted source evidence; a persistent cache avoids re-interpreting unchanged candidates across scheduled runs, with cursor-based batching so large candidate sets are processed incrementally.
- **GitHub reconciliation and issue filing**: resolves referenced issues/PRs, checks for existing open or previously-closed tracking issues, and files issues with the `stale-issue-detection` and `cookie` labels. Filing is capped at 5 total open tracking issues at a time; once that many are open, filing halts until a human closes some of them.

The Issue Monster workflow will then pick up these new issues, due to the `cookie` label, and start fixing them.

Fixes: #56121
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open PR "Add an agent workflow to identify potentially stale references in Ignore attributes, TODOs, and workarounds" (#56405)

Issues.Title: Update common project templates to net12.0
Issues.Body:
🤖 Moves the bundled common project templates to .NET 12. This follows the net11 update pattern (dotnet/dotnet#3873 and 899272c73d). It is opened early to see what passes before the stage0 SDK update, which isn't possible yet.

## Changes
- **Package/folder:** `template_feed/Microsoft.DotNet.Common.ProjectTemplates.11.0` renamed to `12.0` (folder, csproj, PackageId), with references updated in `sdk.slnx`, `source-build.slnf` and `TemplateEngine.slnf`.
- **Identity/precedence:** all template identities use the `.12.0` suffix, and precedence goes from 13000 to 14000.
- **Content:**
  - ClassLibrary, Console, NUnit, xUnit and Playwright-NUnit now target `net12.0`, and their display strings say ".NET 12.0". This includes a few localized strings that still said ".NET 10.0".
  - MSTest and Playwright-MSTest already offer net12.0 and net11.0 choices, so only the default/replaced framework changed. The choice lists are untouched.
- **Tests:**
  - `dotnet-new.IntegrationTests` now references the 11.0 Common and Web template packages. Scenarios that installed the 10.0 package now install 11.0, and the F#/VB MSTest cases use net11.0.
  - The approvals move to net12.0. The WebProjectsTests approvals are unchanged because they come from the aspnetcore templates.

## Notes for reviewers
- User-visible: `dotnet new console`, `classlib` and the test templates now default to `net12.0`.
- The class-template and instantiate tests may fail until stage0 understands net12.0.

Issues.Title: Add workflow to identify stale Ignore attributes
Issues.Body:
## Summary

- add a weekly agentic workflow that finds MSTest `[Ignore(...)]` attributes linked to completed GitHub issues or merged pull requests
- file at most three deduplicated tracking issues per run using a stable source-path and fully qualified test marker
- label generated issues with `agentic-workflows`, `Test Debt`, and `cookie` so Issue Monster can revalidate them
- keep discovery conservative: all gating references must be resolved, and the workflow never assumes the ignored test now passes

This adapts the approach from microsoft/testfx#9251 to the issue-first flow requested by the SDK repository.

## Validation

- compiled `.github/workflows/stale-ignore-tracker.md` in strict mode
- confirmed the generated workflow is current with `gh-aw status`
- verified telemetry correlation, safe-output labels, write permissions, and immutable action pins in the generated lock
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #56121

Issues.Title: Measure CLI activities and MSBuild submission durations
Issues.Body:
Implements [Chet's activity-based proposal](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/pull/55499#discussion_r3936764697) as an alternative to #55499.

- Adds activities for MSBuild invocation, Pack/Publish release-settings discovery, and run/test project, device, framework, and environment preparation.
- Exposes existing and new CLI activity durations through the `dotnet-cli` meter's `dotnet.cli.activity.duration` histogram: seconds, tagged by `activity.name`, using existing collection/export configuration.
- Adds focused tests for metric values and execution boundaries, including actual MSBuild calls.

These are inclusive phase timings, **not a single startup-to-first-submission measurement**. Preparatory phases can themselves perform MSBuild work.

Issues.Body:
> This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10569. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the release of .NET 11 Release Candidate 1. Follow the main announcement and [blog announcement](https://aka.ms/dotnet/11/rc1).

This is our first of two release candidates which come with a [go-live support license](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/dotnet-core#previews) so you can confidently use this release for your production applications. This release of .NET 11 is supported in the new [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/) release alongside Visual Studio Code with the C# Dev Kit. Check out the full release notes below and get started today.

This release contains the following highlights and improvements.

Browse the release notes for a full list of improvements in this release:

- [.NET MAUI](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/dotnetmaui.md)
- [ASP.NET Core](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/aspnetcore.md)
- [C#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/csharp.md)
- [F#](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/fsharp.md)
- [Container images](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/containers.md)
- [EF Core & Data](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/efcore.md)
- [Libraries](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/libraries.md)
- [MSBuild](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)
- [NuGet](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/nuget.md)
- [Runtime](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/runtime.md)
- [SDK](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/sdk.md)
- [Windows Forms](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/winforms.md)

## Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, we recommend installing the latest [Visual Studio 2026 Insiders](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/insiders/). You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 | ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69304 – ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core IIS out-of-process hosting and request decompression. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The IIS Middleware for ASP.NET Core did not properly constrain decompression of certain types of request, leading to excess memory consumption and a Denial of Service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/69155 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-409 (Improper Handling of Highly Compressed Data (Data Amplification)) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows / IIS out-of-process - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 11 RC1 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-rc.1 | 11.0.0-rc.1 version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 [Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.AspNetCore.App.Runtime.win-arm64) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.30 | 8.0.31 If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. If you have installed one or more .NET SDKs through Visual Studio, Visual Studio will prompt you to update Visual Studio, which will also update your .NET SDKs. 2. If your application references the vulnerable package, update the package reference to the patched version. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated runtime or SDK, restart your apps for the update to take effect. Issues.Body: # Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-69806 – .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET SDK dotnet watch. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. The dotnet-watch AspireServerService exposes information through the use of certain arguments, that in turn can enable code injection. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/56167 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.0 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-200 (Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor); CWE-94 (Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux - **Architectures:** All ## Affected .NET SDKs The vulnerability affects Linux installations of the .NET SDK in the version ranges listed below. These are SDK versions, not NuGet package versions. ### .NET 11 RC1 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 11.0.1xx RC1 | Earlier .NET 11 previews | 11.0.100-rc.1 ### .NET 10 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 10.0.1xx | >= 10.0.100, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 10.0.3xx | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.399 | 10.0.400 ### .NET 9 SDK feature band | Affected SDK version | Patched SDK version ---------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- 9.0.3xx | >= 9.0.300, <= 9.0.316 | 9.0.317 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using an SDK listed in [affected .NET SDKs](#affected-sdks) on Linux, you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? 1. To fix the issue please install the latest version of .NET. 2. Update each affected SDK feature band to the patched version listed above. You can list the versions you have installed by running the `dotnet --info` command. Once you have installed the updated SDK, restart dotnet watch and your applications for the update to take effect. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-62900 | .NET Information Disclosure Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git and Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git. This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. Improper removal of sensitive information before storage or transfer in .NET allows an unauthorized attacker to disclose information over a network. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sourcelink/issues/1757 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 5.9 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-212: Improper Removal of Sensitive Information Before Storage or Transfer ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### Published NuGet packages Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | = 8.0.0 | No patched NuGet version; update to a fixed .NET 8 SDK [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.102, <= 10.0.110 | 10.0.111 [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.200, <= 10.0.204 | No patched NuGet version; the 10.0.2xx SDK feature band is no longer serviced [Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SourceLink.AzureRepos.Git) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.301 | 10.0.303 The affected packages used by .NET 8 and .NET 9 SDKs are built with SDK-specific prerelease versions that aren't published as stable NuGet packages. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that causes uncontrolled resource consumption, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130714 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-770 (Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-50527 | .NET Denial of Service Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET XML Encryption (System.Security.Cryptography.Xml). This advisory also provides guidance on what developers can do to update their applications to remove this vulnerability. A denial of service vulnerability exists in the XML encryption implementation (EncryptedXml) in .NET 8, .NET 9, and .NET 10. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by supplying crafted encrypted XML that is improperly validated, resulting in denial of service. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/130712 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-121 (Stack-based Buffer Overflow) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** All - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The vulnerability affects any Microsoft .NET project if it uses any of affected package versions listed below ### .NET 10.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.9 | 10.0.10 ### .NET 9.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.17 | 9.0.18 ### .NET 8.0 Package name | Affected version | Patched version ------------ | ---------------- | ------------------------- [System.Security.Cryptography.Xml](https://www.nuget.org/packages/System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.3 | 8.0.4 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? If using a package listed in [affected packages](#affected-packages), you're exposed to the vulnerability. ### How do I fix the issue? To update the System.Security.Cryptography.Xml NuGet package, use one of the following methods: NuGet Package Manager UI in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Right-click on your project in Solution Explorer and select "Manage NuGet Packages..." or navigate to "Project > Manage NuGet Packages". - In the NuGet Package Manager window, select the "Updates" tab. This tab lists packages with available updates from your configured package sources. - Select the package(s) you wish to update. You can choose a specific version from the dropdown or update to the latest available version. - Click the "Update" button. Using the NuGet Package Manager Console in Visual Studio: - Open your project in Visual Studio. - Navigate to "Tools > NuGet Package Manager > Package Manager Console". - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following Update-Package command: ```Update-Package -Id System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Using the .NET CLI (Command Line Interface): - Open a terminal or command prompt in your project's directory. - To update a specific package to its latest version, use the following add package command: ```dotnet add package System.Security.Cryptography.Xml``` Once you have updated the nuget package reference you must recompile and deploy your application. Additionally we recommend you update your runtime and/or SDKs, but it is not necessary to patch the vulnerability. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization.
